title: Eighth Word Religion And Worldly Life Choosing Between Two Roads

questions.question: According to the opening of the passage, what two phrases are presented as the key to solving the world's mystery and rescuing the human spirit from darkness?
questions.answer: Calling on Allah and affirming His oneness.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to the world if true religion is absent?
questions.answer: It becomes like a prison.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the human condition without religion?
questions.answer: Human beings become the most miserable of creatures.

questions.question: In the comparison, what did the two brothers ask the serious man at the fork in the road?
questions.answer: They asked which path was better.

questions.question: How did the man describe the path on the right?
questions.answer: It required discipline and obedience, but it led to safety and well-being.

questions.question: How did the man describe the path on the left?
questions.answer: It offered freedom from restraint, but it led to danger and misery.

questions.question: Which brother chose the right path, and what inner quality is linked to that choice?
questions.answer: The brother with good character chose it, and his choice is linked to trust in Allah and moral uprightness.

questions.question: Why did the other brother choose the left path?
questions.answer: He wanted a way without restrictions and was driven by laziness and bad character.

questions.question: What contrast does the passage make between how the left-hand road first seemed and what it really was?
questions.answer: It looked easy on the surface, but it was actually heavy and difficult.

questions.question: What main lesson about religion and human life is introduced before the story of the two brothers begins?
questions.answer: True religion gives meaning, freedom from darkness, and a way out of misery, while life without it traps and harms the human spirit.

questions.question: What larger subjects does the passage say can be understood through the comparison that follows?
questions.answer: The world, the human spirit, the place of religion in human life, and why life without true religion becomes miserable.

questions.question: What Qur'anic truths are stated before the comparison begins?
questions.answer: Allah alone is worthy of worship, He is living and sustaining all, and Islam is the religion accepted before Him.

questions.question: Where were the brothers when they met the serious-looking man?
questions.answer: They were at a place where the road split into two directions.

questions.question: What choice was placed before them by the man at the fork?
questions.answer: They had to choose between an ordered path with effort and a lawless path with apparent ease.

questions.question: What does the right-hand path suggest about the relationship between limits and human good?
questions.answer: Limits can protect a person and lead to peace and happiness.

questions.question: What does the left-hand path suggest about unrestricted freedom?
questions.answer: Freedom without guidance can bring harm, instability, and suffering.

questions.question: What words did the good brother say before taking the right path, and what do those words show?
questions.answer: He expressed reliance on Allah, which shows trust and submission.

questions.question: How is the second brother morally described in contrast to the first?
questions.answer: He is portrayed as undisciplined and morally weak, unlike the upright first brother.

questions.question: Why does the passage invite the reader to follow the second brother first?
questions.answer: To show that what looks comfortable at first can actually become a burden.

questions.question: What is the main contrast set up by the opening scene of the comparison?
questions.answer: One way joins obedience with safety, while the other joins self-indulgence with ruin.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person will understand if he reflects carefully on the comparison?
questions.answer: He will understand the meaning of the world, the human spirit, and the necessity of true religion.

questions.question: According to the passage, what delivers the human spirit from darkness?
questions.answer: Turning to Allah and affirming that only He is God.

questions.question: In the comparison, what kind of journey do the brothers begin?
questions.answer: They begin a long journey.

questions.question: What was the first major decision they had to make on that journey?
questions.answer: They had to choose between two different roads.

questions.question: What burden comes with the right road?
questions.answer: A person must live under order, law, and restraint.

questions.question: What benefit comes with that burden?
questions.answer: It brings security and happiness.

questions.question: What attraction comes with the left road?
questions.answer: It seems open and unrestricted.

questions.question: What hidden cost comes with the left road?
questions.answer: It leads to danger and wretchedness.

questions.question: How does the response of the good brother reveal his mindset before he starts walking?
questions.answer: He begins with trust in Allah and accepts guidance rather than relying on his own impulses.

questions.question: What early judgment does the passage make about the second brother’s choice?
questions.answer: His path only appears easy, but in truth it is oppressive and hard.

questions.question: What does the passage connect with understanding the value of religion for human beings?
questions.answer: It connects religion with understanding both the world and the human soul.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the condition of the world when true religion is missing?
questions.answer: It is like a place of confinement rather than real freedom.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the spiritual effect of saying “O Allah” and declaring Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: These turn a person toward truth and bring light to the inner life.

questions.question: What simple story framework is used to explain these ideas?
questions.answer: A comparison between two brothers taking different roads.

questions.question: What role does the serious-looking man play in the story?
questions.answer: He explains the consequences of each road before the brothers choose.

questions.question: In moral terms, how are the two roads different?
questions.answer: One is shaped by discipline and protection, while the other is shaped by unchecked freedom and harm.

questions.question: What does the better brother do after hearing the warning about the roads?
questions.answer: He entrusts himself to Allah and follows the regulated path.

questions.question: What does the worse brother value more than safety or happiness?
questions.answer: He values being unrestrained.

questions.question: Why is the left road not truly easier according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because the comfort it promises hides deeper hardship.

questions.question: What broad lesson does this opening comparison teach about guidance?
questions.answer: Divine guidance may ask for self-control, but it leads to real peace, while rejecting guidance leads to suffering.

questions.question: What three big themes are named before the comparison starts?
questions.answer: The nature of the world, the reality of the human spirit, and the importance of religion for human beings.

questions.question: What does the passage say religion prevents the world from becoming for a person?
questions.answer: A prison.

questions.question: Without religion, what kind of state does the passage say human beings fall into?
questions.answer: A state of extreme misery.

questions.question: What action begins the comparison between the two brothers?
questions.answer: They set out together on a long trip.

questions.question: What information did they seek from the man they met at the split in the road?
questions.answer: Guidance about which way was the better one to take.

questions.question: What is paired together on the right side of the fork?
questions.answer: Obligation and order are paired with security and happiness.

questions.question: What is paired together on the left side of the fork?
questions.answer: Lack of restraint is paired with danger and unhappiness.

questions.question: What does the good brother’s choice show about his relationship to guidance?
questions.answer: He is willing to accept guidance and live within rightful limits.

questions.question: What does the bad brother’s choice show about his desires?
questions.answer: He prefers immediate ease and freedom from rules over what is truly good.

questions.question: Why does the passage say we follow the second brother in imagination?
questions.answer: So we can see how a seemingly easy path can become painful in reality.

questions.question: What does the passage say someone can come to understand about religion if he listens to the comparison?
questions.answer: He can understand its true worth for human life and why it saves a person from misery.

questions.question: Which religion is named as the one accepted before Allah in this passage?
questions.answer: Islam.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use to describe life in the world without true religion?
questions.answer: It compares it to imprisonment.

questions.question: What is the spiritual result of calling on Allah and affirming His oneness, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The inner human being is rescued from darkness.

questions.question: In the story, what choice stands before the two brothers?
questions.answer: They must choose between a disciplined road and an unrestricted road.

questions.question: Why is the road on the right not simply a road of hardship?
questions.answer: Because its discipline protects a person and leads to peace and happiness.

questions.question: Why is the road on the left not truly a road of freedom?
questions.answer: Because its lack of restraint ends in danger and misery.

questions.question: What personal quality is especially emphasized in the brother who takes the right path?
questions.answer: Good character.

questions.question: What personal flaws are emphasized in the brother who takes the left path?
questions.answer: He is immoral and lazy.

questions.question: What central contrast does the final sentence of the target passage underline about appearances?
questions.answer: What seems easy may actually be burdensome, and what seems demanding may be the safer and better way.
